description: What Orchard Core is, installing a first site, and finding your way around the admin.
Creating, finding, previewing, scheduling and cleaning up content items.
Modeling content: types, parts and their settings, from the admin and from code.
The built-in content fields, their editors, and relating content items.
The smaller built-in parts: titles, aliases, custom site settings.
Containers of content items: blogs, news, galleries.
Building pages from widgets with the Flow and Bag parts.
Categorizing content with taxonomies, terms and tags.
The media library, media fields, profiles, security and storage.
Menus for visitors, and how themes render navigation.
URLs of content items, the home page, and URL rewriting.
Search engine optimization, sitemaps, feeds and analytics.
Choosing and creating themes for the front end and the admin.
Liquid templates, shortcodes and overriding shapes from the admin.
How Orchard Core renders a page: shapes, alternates and placement.
Widgets in zones, shown by layers and their rules.
Indexes, search providers and the front-end search page.
Saved queries over indexes and the database, and where to use them.
Automating tasks with workflows: events, tasks, HTTP, timers.
User accounts, sign-in, registration and profiles.
Roles, permissions and content-level access.
Hardening a site: HTTPS, headers, CORS, bots, rate limits.
One secure home for passwords, API keys and certificates.
Who changed what, when, and restoring earlier versions.
Signing in with Microsoft, Google, Meta, GitHub and X accounts.
Orchard Core as an identity provider, and as a client of one.
Multilingual sites: cultures, translated content and translated UI.
Setting up and updating sites from recipe files.
Moving configuration and content between environments.
Running many sites from one application.
Querying content with GraphQL.
Decoupled and headless sites, REST endpoints and API documentation.
Sending email and text messages, and notifying users.
Building forms from widgets and processing what visitors submit.
Exporting, transforming and importing data with pipelines.
Caching, compression, profiling and background tasks.
Error pages, health checks, logs and telemetry.
Configuration, data, data protection and running at scale.
Writing modules: parts, fields, drivers, settings, steps and activities.
Cross-feature walkthroughs that build a whole site, step by step.
